title: Fasten a bracelet on a wrist form
instruction: Fasten the bracelet around the wrist form, then let go and leave it secure.
context: Helping someone fasten small jewellery requires holding a flexible band, aligning its clasp and closing it without dropping either end. This trial uses a rigid wrist form.
setup: A 22 cm long, 54 mm diameter rigid silicone wrist form lies horizontally on two 25 x 80 x 25 mm plastic end supports. The middle remains clear underneath. A blue leather band, 210 x 10 x 2 mm, lies flat below its midpoint with the two clasp ends 21 cm apart. Its silver push-in pin clasp has two 10 x 7 mm housings and a 6 mm projecting pin. Both robot hands start open. Use the fixed layout and clasp orientations in the setup photograph.
scoring: 1.0 if the clasp is closed, the intact bracelet surrounds the wrist form within 5 cm of its midpoint, and both hands have released it for three seconds. 0.5 if it is closed around the form but still held. 0.25 if the pin has entered the socket by at least 1 mm but has not caught. Otherwise 0. A broken, overstretched or off-wrist bracelet scores 0. Inspect the clasp and released bracelet with photographs and a ruler.
fidelity: The robot, rigid wrist form, supports and cameras use native PhysX. The leather is a coarse flexible, length-constrained chain with gravity and wrist contact. Visible clasp grips are idealized captures. The pin and socket require geometric alignment and insertion before a simplified spring catch engages. Leather stretch failure, misalignment and release can prevent success. Detailed spring deformation, resolved finger friction and forces back onto the arms are omitted; this is not a calibrated jewellery model.
reset_notes: Open the clasp and restore the flat band, form and hands to the photographed layout. Nothing is consumed.
